clue.text: After most of month I take alternative lower rank

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter is kept here

parts.note: June is a month of the year
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A soldier, past the start of a month, chooses another path to a lower rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the month's last letter; 'After' and 'take' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior is someone holding a lower position or grade than others in an organisation.

clue.text: On good terms with class, head regularly knowing enough

parts.note: to be well in with someone is to be on good terms with them
a form is a school class

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word head, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Being friendly with the class and its headteacher keeps one informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'head', giving ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-informed has ample knowledge of a subject, knowing as much as is needed.

clue.text: At which point our nephew cracked up

indicators.note: cracked up suggests something broken into pieces, so the letters of our nephew are rearranged

explanation.surface: The moment when a family's nephew had a breakdown, or burst out laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked up' rearranges OURNEPHEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Whereupon is a conjunction meaning immediately after which, marking the moment something happened.

clue.text: Protected, like a building like one in Pisa

definitions.meaning: a ... building in Britain is legally protected from demolition or alteration because of its historic value
the Leaning Tower of Pisa leans, and to list is to lean to one side

explanation.surface: Heritage protection, as enjoyed by a famous Italian tower.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'listed building' is a British term for a building on an official heritage register.
explanation.definitionFit: Listed means officially protected as a heritage building, and also tilting, as ships and towers do.

clue.text: Desperately recruit next man to bring in old form of assessment?

indicators.note: to bring in means the jumbled letters take the next piece inside them
desperately suggests wild, frantic action, so the letters of recruit next man are jumbled

explanation.surface: An urgent plea to hire another person to deal with an outdated form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperately' scrambles RECRUITNEXTMAN, and 'to bring in' places O inside that jumble; the question mark flags the pun on 'form' and tax 'assessment'.
explanation.definitionFit: An income tax return is the official document by which a taxpayer's liability is assessed.

clue.text: Deceive having hand cover that's a bloomer!

parts.note: to fox someone is to baffle or deceive them
a glove covers the hand

explanation.surface: Fooling someone with a glove on would be quite the blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A foxglove is a flowering plant, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Loud wordy exchanges

indicators.note: exchanges suggests swapping places, so the letters of wordy change position

explanation.surface: Noisy, long-winded arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanges' rearranges WORDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdy describes noisy and disorderly behaviour, a near synonym of loud.

clue.text: Astonishingly, April due to give back number

indicators.note: astonishingly suggests something surprising happening, so the letters of April due are rearranged

explanation.surface: Remarkably, an old magazine issue is to be returned in April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Astonishingly' rearranges APRILDUE. 'back number' reads as an old magazine issue, but it is something that numbs the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidural is an anaesthetic injected near the spine, deadening sensation in the lower body.

clue.text: Any number leaving, eat a large quantity

indicators.note: leaving means that letter departs from the word it was in

parts.note: to munch is to eat
N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: After a crowd departs, one eats a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes N from MUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Much is used as a noun for a great amount, as in 'much of it'.

clue.text: Officer of business cross with lover

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
X is a cross
a swain is an old word for a suitor or lover

explanation.surface: A company official angry with a romantic partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry but gives the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxswain is the officer in charge of a ship's boat, or a petty officer steering a vessel.

clue.text: Trio belt out part of opera

indicators.note: out suggests things are wrong or disordered, so the letters of trio belt are rearranged

explanation.surface: Three singers loudly perform a section of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TRIOBELT; 'belt out' reads as singing loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the written text of an opera, sung by the performers.

clue.text: Amateur excluded from sketch

parts.note: lay means non-professional, as in a layman
out means left out or excluded

explanation.surface: A non-professional was dropped from a comedy sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sketch' reads as a comedy piece but here means a rough plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A layout is a planned arrangement, like a rough drawing showing how things are positioned.

clue.text: Worn down, having nothing for new beginning

parts.note: ground means worn down by grinding
zero means nothing

explanation.surface: Exhausted and with nothing left, someone must start afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground zero is idiomatically the starting point from which something is rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground zero is used for a fresh starting point, as in going back to square one.

clue.text: Drip returning, normal to remove front of optics?

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for a drip is read backwards

parts.note: a drip is an intravenous feed, abbreviated IV

indicators.note: to remove front means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: usual means normal

explanation.surface: A hospital drip comes back, and normal practice drops the front lens of an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns IV into VI; 'to remove front' takes U off USUAL to give SUAL. 'front of optics' looks like O, but 'of optics?' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Visual means relating to sight, which is what optics concerns.

clue.text: Second rug removed and purloined

indicators.note: removed suggests letters moved from their places, so second and rug are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A second rug was taken away and stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges SECONDRUG; 'Second' looks like S but is used whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrounge is to obtain something by cadging or taking it, close to purloining.

clue.text: Final defeat that's the end of the line?

definitions.meaning: to meet one's ... is to suffer a final defeat, after Napoleon at the Battle of ...
London ... is a railway terminus, where lines end

explanation.surface: A defeat that finishes things for good.
explanation.walkthrough: London Waterloo is a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo, Napoleon's last battle, became a byword for a decisive defeat; the station is where trains terminate.

clue.text: American generation's normal practice

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US citizen
an age is a generation or era

explanation.surface: The customary habits of a generation of Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the way something is habitually done.

clue.text: Not going with the current trend

definitions.text: Not going with the current trend

parts.words: Not going with the current trend
parts.note: reads as being a nonconformist, but literally means moving against the flow of a river

explanation.surface: Someone bucking fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstream means travelling against the river's flow, opposite to the current.

clue.text: Forty winks Felix has?

definitions.meaning: forty winks is a short sleep
Felix is a famous cartoon cat

explanation.surface: A short doze taken by a cat named Felix.
explanation.walkthrough: Felix the Cat is a classic cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a brief light sleep, the kind cats are famous for taking.

clue.text: Bursars got disorganised in the city

indicators.note: disorganised means the letters of bursars got are put in a new, untidy order

explanation.surface: University finance officers became muddled in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorganised' rearranges BURSARSGOT; 'got' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Strasbourg is a city in north-eastern France, seat of the European Parliament.

clue.text: Never mind runner on top of mine

indicators.note: in a down answer, on top of means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a ski is a runner that slides over snow
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Forget about the athlete standing on a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete, but a ski is a runner on snow, like a sledge runner.
explanation.definitionFit: Skip it is an idiom telling someone to forget the matter, much as never mind does.

clue.text: Part of affair is questionably indecent

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something about the affair is dubiously improper.
explanation.definitionFit: Risqué describes something slightly improper or sexually suggestive.

clue.text: Leave river holding record

indicators.note: holding means the river's name wraps around the record

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon, England
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Go away from the river while keeping a record.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dart is a river in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart is to go away, which is to leave.

clue.text: Own up now Frenchman has sex appeal

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the present era, so it can stand for now
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Confess that the Frenchman is attractive these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal comes from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to confess it, which is owning up.

clue.text: Most wishy-washy from pub included by the way

indicators.note: included by means the pub goes inside the words that follow

parts.note: an inn is a pub
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: The feeblest drink from the pub along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like a throwaway phrase, but 'the' and 'way' both give letters, and 'included by' places the pub between their first two letters and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinnest means most watery or diluted, the weakest in consistency or character.

clue.text: Simple type dressed in iron with gold torch

indicators.note: dressed in means the simple type is clothed by the iron symbol around it

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a lamb is an innocent, simple person
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A naive person in iron armour and gold carries a flame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed in' has the iron symbol clothe the simple type; a lamb stands for an innocent, guileless person.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, especially one made of thick wicks dipped in wax.

clue.text: Case of free tuition

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the answer is a run of letters within free tuition

explanation.surface: An instance of lessons given at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of' looks like an instance, but Case is the definition and 'of' marks letters taken out of the next words.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: Infected? No admittance unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong, so the letters of no admittance are rearranged

explanation.surface: Refused entry to a hospital ward because one might be carrying disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges NOADMITTANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Contaminated means polluted or tainted by germs, as an infected wound is.
